classification.difficultyReason: Track countries through the legend, estimate a crossing year between plotted dates and compare total endpoint decreases rather than simply ranking final rates.

content.prompt:
The following line graphs represent the estimated and projected illiteracy rates of selected countries from 1970 to 2015.

(Source: www.uis.unesco.org/en/stats/statistics/UIS_Literacy_Country2002.xls, accessed 8 April 2006)

spec.description: All six ten-point series reconstructed from original PDF line vectors; symbols and legend distinguish Cambodia, China, Singapore, Vietnam, Niger and Oman. Values are graphical estimates, not newly asserted survey precision.
spec.mathematics: Percentage0–100 at ten five-year positions1970–2015; vector-derived Oman–Cambodia crossing1995.889, consistent with approximately1996.
spec.answerVisibility: Given source graph; no answer annotations.

children.label: a
children.prompt: In which country is the illiteracy rate projected to be the lowest in the year 2015?

answer.worked: At 2015, Singapore’s plotted point is the lowest of the six countries.

children.label: b
children.prompt: In which country is the illiteracy rate projected to be the highest in the year 2015?

answer.worked: At 2015, Niger’s plotted point is the highest of the six countries.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Estimate the year when the illiteracy rate for Oman fell below that of Cambodia.

answer.worked: The Oman and Cambodia lines cross just after 1995. Reading the year at this intersection gives approximately 1996.

children.label: d
children.prompt: In which country has the illiteracy rate fallen the most?

answer.worked: Compare each country’s decrease from 1970 to 2015. Oman falls from about 82% to about 13%, the largest decrease.

children.label: e
children.prompt: In which country has the illiteracy rate fallen the least?

answer.worked: Compare each country’s decrease from 1970 to 2015. Vietnam falls from about 17% to about 5%, the smallest decrease.
